studies.Study: Ben Fradj MK et al. (2018) [PMID: 30183426] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Decreased Oleic Acid and Marine n - 3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids in Tunisian Patients with Urothelial Bladder Cancer.
studies.Title: Decreased Oleic Acid and Marine n - 3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids in Tunisian Patients with Urothelial Bladder Cancer.
studies.Authors: Ben Fradj MK, Ouanes Y, Hadj-Taieb S, Sallemi A, Kallel A, Jemaa R, Kaabachi N, Nouira Y, Feki M
studies.Population: Patients with urothelial bladder cancer and controls
studies.comparison_type: third tertile vs first tertile of plasma eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)

sample_size.excerpt: A case-control study including 250 patients with urothelial bladder cancer (UBC) and 250 controls was conducted.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 250 + 250 = 500

cases.excerpt: A case-control study including 250 patients with urothelial bladder cancer (UBC) and 250 controls was conducted.

effect_size.excerpt: first tertile) in oleic [0.54 (0.34-0.86)], dihomo-γ-linolenic (DGLA) [0.47 (0.29-0.74)], eicosapentaenoic (EPA) [0.32 (0.19-0.52)], and docosahexaenoic (DHA) acids [0.33 (0.20-0.53)] were associated with lower risk for UBC.

confidence_interval.excerpt: first tertile) in oleic [0.54 (0.34-0.86)], dihomo-γ-linolenic (DGLA) [0.47 (0.29-0.74)], eicosapentaenoic (EPA) [0.32 (0.19-0.52)], and docosahexaenoic (DHA) acids [0.33 (0.20-0.53)] were associated with lower risk for UBC.

comparison.excerpt: higher levels (third tertile vs. first tertile)

design.excerpt: A case-control study including 250 patients with urothelial bladder cancer (UBC) and 250 controls was conducted.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Plasma FAs composition was assessed using capillary gas chromatography.
